title: The best things to do near The Ambassadors Theatre: Plan your visit to Paranormal Activity
excerpt: Seeing Paranormal Activity in London? Plan your visit with restaurants, bars and things to do near The Ambassadors Theatre
content:
Theatre

Caitlin Devlin / 23 November 2026

Big Day Out

Seeing Paranormal Activity in London? Plan your visit with restaurants, bars, spooky activities and things to do near The Ambassadors Theatre before and after the show.

Planning a visit to Paranormal Activity? We hope you’ve got nerves of steel… Luckily, organising the rest of your day doesn’t have to be scary. From spooky activities to delicious pre-theatre dining, all within a short walk of the theatre, we’ve got you covered.

The Ambassadors Theatre is located on West Street in London’s West End, within easy walking distance of Covent Garden, Leicester Square and Seven Dials. Whether you’re planning a pre-theatre dinner, a spooky activity or post-show drinks, there are plenty of places to visit nearby before and after Paranormal Activity.

The best things to do near The Ambassadors Theatre at a glance:

Best for a quick meal: Seven Dials Market, approximately three minutes’ walk away.
Best for pre-theatre dining: Olea Social, offering Mediterranean dishes near the theatre.
Best for vegetarian and vegan food: Mildreds Covent Garden, approximately five minutes away.
Best free activity: Explore Covent Garden or visit the National Gallery.
Best spooky experience: Try The Curse of Covent Garden before the performance.
Best for post-show drinks: Visit The Two Brewers for a traditional pub experience or Le Beaujolais for a glass of wine.

Plan your visit around Paranormal Activity:


The Ambassadors Theatre has two wheelchair positions on Rows E and G of the Stalls, accessible via a platform lift from the foyer. There is also step-free access to the Stalls. You can find full accessibility information here. Paranormal Activity regularly runs captioned performances – you can check the date of the next captioned performance on their website.

How much time should I allow before seeing Paranormal Activity?

Whether you’re heading straight to the theatre or planning a full day in London’s West End, there’s plenty to do near the Ambassadors Theatre.

If you have 30–60 minutes: Take a quick walk around Covent Garden or Trafalgar Square before heading to the theatre. If you’re hungry, a quick takeaway snack at Seven Dials Market or Chinatown gives you more freedom of time than a sit-down meal.

If you have 1–2 hours: Enjoy a pre-theatre meal at one of our recommended restaurants near the Ambassadors Theatre. Remember to plan to be at the theatre 30 minutes before the performance.

If you have 3–4 hours: Pay a visit to the National Gallery, do some shopping in Covent Garden or brave one of the spooky activities nearby. Sit down for food at one of our recommended restaurants before or after.

If you have a full day: Follow one of our suggested itineraries for the perfect day out, with time for sightseeing, entertainment, dining and drinks before or after Paranormal Activity.

Best restaurants near The Ambassadors Theatre

For pre-theatre dining:

Brother Marcus
2 minutes away | 8am – 10pm | £25 per person
This is a warm, welcoming all-day dining spot, serving seasonal dishes and mezze sharing plates inspired by the flavours of the Eastern Mediterranean. Note that their pre-theatre dining is only an option 4pm – 6pm Monday to Friday. Included is one of their signature Rip & Dip platters to share – fluffy pittas with homemade dips – alongside one vegetable mezze and one meat mezze per person.

For quick and casual dining:

Seven Dials Market
3 minutes away | midday until late (individual vendors vary) | £12 – £15
If you don’t have time for a restaurant meal – or you’ve got a party full of fussy eaters – Seven Dials Market offers over 20 independent food and drink stalls to choose from. Just don’t leave it too late – you’ll need a little time to wait for your food to be prepared, and this popular market can get busy at mealtimes. The prices are a little higher than your average street food stalls, but still a cheaper dinner option than many in the area.

For vegetarian and vegan dining:

Mildreds Covent Garden
5 minutes away | 9am – 11pm | £24/£32 per person
Named London’s favourite vegan restaurant in 2023, Mildreds has long specialised in making vegan food rich in flavour and variety. Their adventurous plant-based menu has global inspirations, and even the most dedicated carnivores will find plenty to enjoy here. Their pre-theatre menu offers two courses for £24 per person, or three for £32.

For something different:

Flesh & Buns
3 minutes away | 12pm – 10/11pm | £25-£60 per person
Below Seven Dials, you’ll find this Izakaya sanctuary, where homemade bao buns meet home-smoked robata fillings, paired with excellent small plates and drinks. Flesh & Buns offer a set menu for £25 per person and a tasting menu for £50 or £60 per person, perfect for anyone looking to celebrate something special.

Our favourite restaurant near the theatre:

Dishoom Covent Garden
1 minute away | 8am – 11pm/12am | £10 – £30 per person (order dependent)
The perfect spot in Covent Garden for a great Indian. In lavish surroundings inspired by the arrival of the Talkies in Indian cinema, you can explore an enormous menu of elevated Bombay street food. Dishoom offers everything from lunch buns and grills to curries and biryanis, covering every aspect of Bombay dining. Vegans, vegetarians and gluten-free diners will all find plenty to enjoy here.

Things to do nearby before Paranormal Activity

The Ambassadors Theatre is in Covent Garden, near a ton of London’s best sightseeing stops. And of course, a trip to Paranormal Activity demands some spooky activities. Here are the best things to do nearby before seeing Paranormal Activity.

  • Covent Garden – Five minutes away. No matter what the weather, Covent Garden offers plenty to see and do, whether you’re exploring the markets, shopping in the boutiques, visiting the Royal Opera House or snapping photos in the Infinity Chamber.
    Open 24 hours (individual attractions and shops vary) | Free to explore
  • Trafalgar Square – Eight minutes away. Weather permitting, we advise putting aside twenty to forty minutes to visit Nelson’s Column and the lions at the fountain. This is one of London’s most iconic sites and a great spot for photos.
    Open 24 hours | Free to explore
  • National Gallery – Eight minutes away. This museum at the edge of Trafalgar Square is free to visit, with a charge for individual exhibits – see what’s on here. If the weather’s not on your side, or if you just want to get lost in some great art, you’ll find works by Uccello, Turner, Van Gogh and many more among this collection of over 1000 paintings. We recommend 1.5 hours to 2.5 hours to explore in-depth, or forty-five to sixty minutes if you’re just looking to take in the highlights.
    Open 10am – 6pm (9pm on Fridays) | Free entry
  • National Portrait Gallery – Seven minutes away. Another free to visit museum, with a charge for individual exhibits – see what’s on here. This collection of portraiture also makes for a great cold/rainy day activity, telling the story of Britain through famous and non-famous faces. We recommend 1.5 to 2 hours for a full visit, and forty-five to sixty minutes for the highlights.
    Open 10:30am – 6pm (9pm on Fridays and Saturdays) | Free entry
  • Neal’s Yard – Three minutes away. Down a side-street you’ll find this unexpected splash of colour. Neal’s Yard is an oasis in the busy West End area, home to a collection of independent cafés, bars and restaurants, as well as the flagship Neal’s Yard Remedies. It’s best seen in the sun but there’s plenty to explore indoors too.
    Open 24 hours (individual business vary) | Free to explore
  • The Curse of Covent Garden – Five minutes away. Looking for something spooky to do before Paranormal Activity? This immersive experience will show you a whole new side to Covent Garden. You and your fellow players will follow nineteen cryptic clues to unravel a dark mystery that has plagued the area for centuries. You can book to play any time within the operational hours – just allow 2 to 3 hours to solve the puzzle.
    Open 9am – 8pm daily | £24 per team.
  • No Escape – Eight minutes away. If you’re ready to be really frightened before Paranormal Activity, you’ve got a choice of two escape rooms on Oxford Street. Can you and your team escape The Demon Barber? Or, if you’re feeling really clever, you might want to take on fiendish villain The Dentist… Allow an hour for either room.
    Open 11am (9:30 on Saturdays and Sundays) – 11pm daily| £40 per person

Best bars and pubs near The Ambassadors Theatre

Traditional pubs:

The Cambridge
2 minutes away | closes 11:30pm – 12am
For a cosy pint, this dark wood-panelled pub is a traditional haunt with a lot of character, built in 1887 on the site of the King’s Arms. Customers particularly enjoy their range of real ales. As with most pubs in the area, you’ll be looking at around £7 per pint.

The Two Brewers
2 minutes away | closes 11 – 11:30pm
This 19th-century pub offers a true link to history, boasting a long history of serving London’s theatrical crowd. They place particular focus on their excellent cask ales. Again, expect to pay around £7 per pint.

Cocktails:

The Escapologist
3 minutes away | closes 12am
This underground bar hides in the old headquarters of a prominent Victorian secret society, serving classic cocktails with a twist. They offer a post-theatre drinks menu, with £8 cocktails if you show your Paranormal Activity ticket.

Baaria
2 minutes away | closes 11pm – 12am (only open late Wed – Sat)
Baaria’s aim is to bring people together Italian-style from sunup to sundown. They’re a café, a wine bar, and most importantly the perfect place to grab a post-show cocktail from their extensive menu. Cocktails and spritzes are about £12.50 per drink, with canapés priced at £3.

Wine bars:

Le Beaujolais
1 minute away | closes 11pm
London’s oldest French wine bar houses a member’s club in its basement, but the ground floor is open to all. The cosy spot works with small French suppliers to bring a real taste of France to London, with prices starting at £6.60 by the glass. From 4:30pm, they operate a walk-ins only system.

La Compagnie
3 minutes away | closes 11-midnight
This hidden gem in Neal’s Yard is set over two floors and a terrace, showcasing the best wines from around the world, with a focus on smaller producers and hard-to-procure bottles. Prices start at £7 by the glass, continuing up to some fairly pricey pours, and reservations are encouraged.

Nightlife:

Dials After Dark
3 minutes away | Friday & Saturday, until late
On Friday and Saturday nights, Seven Dials Market plays host to live acts and DJs in collaboration with Voices Radio. After the show, head on over to listen to the music, soak up the atmosphere and enjoy late-night street food.

The Little Scarlet Door
5 minutes away | closes 1 – 3am
Looking for a great house party in Soho? Look no further – this flat share turned bar and restaurant is the perfect place to dance, drink and unwind after the show, with cocktails starting at £12.

Late night food/dessert:

Chop Chop
5 minutes away | closes 4am
We’re willing to bet this late-night Chinese is a cut above your usual. This contemporary Chinese restaurant inside the Hippodrome Casino showcases the Four Season’s signature meats, with dim sum at £10 – £12 per dish. Since it’s in the casino, all guests have to be over the age of eighteen.

Italian Bear Chocolate
12 minutes away | closes 11pm
This chocolate haven in Soho uses simple and natural ingredients to make the most decadent chocolate creations you’ve ever experienced, perfect for a late-night sweet treat after the show. There’s plenty to love on their menu, but it’s their signature overpoured hot chocolate that you have to try. You’ll pay £6.50 for a regular cup.

Three ways to plan your visit to Paranormal Activity

Head spinning? Here are some example itineraries for your trip to see Paranormal Activity at The Ambassadors Theatre.

For those on a budget:

  • Sightseeing at 2pm – Your afternoon begins visiting the free attractions near the theatre, like Covent Garden, Trafalgar Square and the National Gallery. We recommend bringing a packed lunch that you can enjoy in the Piazza or near the famous lions.
  • Dinner at 5pm – It’s time to head to Seven Dials Market, where you’ve got plenty of time to browse the food stands and choose whatever fits your appetite and budget.
  • Theatre at 7pm – Arrive half an hour before the show begins, grab a drink or a snack, and prepare to be spooked.
  • Drinks at 10pm – After the show, head to The Cambridge for a pint, or The Escapologist for a discounted cocktail.

For date night:

  • A spooky activity at 2pm – If you’re up for turning date night into a date afternoon, The Curse of Covent Garden is the perfect creepy activity to get you in the mood for Paranormal Activity – and get you working as a team.
  • Dinner at 5pm – Brother Marcus’ pre-theatre menu takes care of dinner, and their sharing plates are ideal for date night. (Please note that the pre-theatre menu is not available on Saturdays.) Alternatively, you might want to splash out on the tasting menu at Flesh & Buns.
  • Theatre at 7pm – Arrive half an hour before the show begins, grab a drink or a snack, and prepare to be spooked. You might even want to hold hands…
  • Drinks at 10pm – After the show, walk over to Le Beaujolais for a romantic glass of wine, or to Italian Bear Chocolate to share their chocolate covered strawberries.

For a matinée:

  • Theatre at 2pm – Arrive half an hour before the show begins, grab a drink or a snack, and prepare to be spooked.
  • Dinner at 5pm – After the show, grab an early dinner at Dishoom. With no time constraints, you’re free to explore the extensive menu.  
  • A scary escape room at 7pm – Now that you’ve calmed your nerves again, it’s time to get back on theme and head to No Escape for a frightening challenge.
  • Drinks and live music at 8:30pm – Head over to Seven Dials Market for Dials After Dark, where you can enjoy the live entertainment alongside drinks and a late-night snack.

How to get to the Ambassador’s Theatre

Travelling by tube: The closest tube station to The Ambassadors Theatre is Leicester Square (Piccadilly and Northern lines), a five-minute walk away. Other stations within a ten/fifteen-minute walk include Covent Garden (Piccadilly line), Charing Cross (Northern/Bakerloo line), Tottenham Court Road (Central, Northern and Elizabeth lines) and Piccadilly Circus (Piccadilly line). For step-free access, use Tottenham Court Road Station.

Travelling by train: The closest train station to The Ambassadors Theatre is Charing Cross, which is a ten-minute walk away. Whilst the tube station at Charing Cross is not fully accessible, the train station does have step-free access.  

Travelling by bus: The following bus routes drop off near Cambridge Circus, a two-minute walk from the theatre: 14, 19, 24, 29, 38 or 176.

Travelling by car: Q-Park Chinatown and Covent Garden Car Park are both within a ten-minute walk of the theatre. Make sure to book in advance to secure your spot.

Travelling by coach: Victoria Coach Station is a forty-four-minute walk from the theatre, or a thirty-five to forty-minute bus journey on the 10, 19 or 24. You can also access the coach station by taking the tube to Victoria Station and then walking for nine minutes.

We recommend planning your route with TFL.

Other spooky activities in London

If you have more time to kill in the capital, here are some Paranormal Activity-themed activities that will take you beyond the West End.

The London Dungeon: Westminster
London’s most famous scary attraction combines live acting, spooky storytelling and special effects to transport you back in time to the city’s murkiest moments. Spanning a thousand years of history, you’ll explore Guy Fawkes’ gunpowder plot, Jack The Ripper’s gory secrets and lots more, as you enjoy an experience that inspired both laughs and screams.
Open daily from 10am – 5pm (often 7pm on Fridays) | From £35 per person | Riverside Building, County Hall, Westminster Bridge Rd, London SE1 7PB

The Tower of London: Tower Hill.
You can see the Crown Jewels and the famous White Tower at this historic site, but the spook-factor lies in the Yeoman Warder tour, where you’ll hear tales of intrigue, imprisonment, execution, torture and more.
Open daily from 9am (10am Sun & Mon) – 4:30pm | £38 per person | Tower of London, London, EC3N 4AB

Jack The Ripper Walking Tour: Whitechapel
Regarded as the best Ripper tour in the city, this walking tour uses RIPPER-VISION – handheld projectors that emblazon five foot images upon the dark streets and alleyways of Whitechapel – to transport you back in time, as you walk the very route the Ripper would have taken. It’s an hour and forty-five minutes of thrills.
Running at 5pm Thursday – Sunday and 7:30pm daily | £21 per person | 88 Whitechapel High Street, London, E1 7QX

The London Ghost Bus Tour: Westminster.
A vintage Routemaster bus, a creepy conductor and a tour packed full of London’s haunted secrets… This is the perfect activity to do the day before or after seeing Paranormal Activity – or even straight after a matinée. You’ll spend seventy-five minutes (traffic allowing) touring haunted hotspots around Westminster Abbey, Fleet Street and London Bridge.
Running at 7:30pm and 9pm daily | from £17 per person | 8 Northumberland Avenue, London, WC2N 5BY
